title: Analysis of Motor Signatures of Social Adaptation in Autism for Efficient Human-Centric Systems
abstract: arXiv:2608.12548v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Dance imitation integrates motor planning, sensorimotor integration, and social cognition, offering a sensitive framework to characterize motor behavior in autism. In this work, we explore a computational analysis framework to identify potential biomarkers that allow the design and development of improved medical and human-machine systems. We analyzed 3D motion capture data from autistic and neurotypical adults performing dance imitation under solo and socially-framed duo conditions. Methodologically, using Dynamic Time Warping, we quantified movement consistency and propose the Social Context Sensitivity Index (SCSI) to measure modulation of variability by social framing. These features were then used on a classifier to discriminate subjects into autistic or neurotypical groups. translated_title: 自闭症社会适应运动特征分析：面向高效人本系统
translated_abstract: 舞蹈模仿整合了运动规划、感觉运动整合和社会认知，为表征自闭症运动行为提供了敏感框架。在本研究中，我们探索了一种计算分析框架，以识别潜在生物标志物，从而支持改进医疗和人机系统的设计与开发。我们分析了自闭症和神经典型成年人在独舞和社交框架下的双人舞蹈模仿中的三维动作捕捉数据。方法上，使用动态时间规整量化运动一致性，并提出社会情境敏感性指数（SCSI）来测量社会框架对变异性调节的影响。这些特征随后用于分类器，以区分自闭症或神经典型受试者。结果显示，神经典型成年人在社交框架模仿中表现出更高的运动变异性，尤其是在上肢和下肢，而自闭症受试者则表现出降低的变异性。
tldr: 本文提出社会情境敏感性指数（SCSI）作为生物标志物，通过分析舞蹈模仿中的运动变异性，有效区分自闭症与神经典型个体，为人本医疗和机器系统设计提供支持。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the Social Context Sensitivity Index (SCSI) as a biomarker, distinguishing autistic from neurotypical individuals via dance imitation variability, supporting human-centric medical and machine system design.
